title: Regional Product Manager - IMEA Lead Logistics Product
description:
The Regional Product Manager – Lead Logistics is part of a team that is responsible for driving profitable growth, customer retention, product performance, and operational excellence across the regional Lead Logistics portfolio.

The role works across commercial, customer experience, operations, finance, procurement, technology, and global product teams to strengthen the existing customer portfolio, accelerate business growth, improve financial and operational performance, and drive adoption of scalable product capabilities.

The position requires a strong combination of commercial acumen, analytical capability, customer orientation, and cross-functional leadership. The role holder will lead strategic initiatives without necessarily having direct authority over all contributing teams and must therefore be able to influence effectively across a matrix area, regional and global stakeholder network.

Key Responsibilities

1. Existing Customer Growth and Retention

  • Support the development and execution of the Same Store Sales and customer renewal strategy across the Lead Logistics portfolio.
  • Own and drive structured renewal planning for assigned customer segments, including opportunity identification, risk assessment, stakeholder alignment, and action tracking.
  • Develop and maintain renewal playbooks, frameworks, governance mechanisms, and supporting tools.
  • Partner with customer and commercial teams to identify retention risks and develop mitigation plans.
  • Support cross-regional customer growth and renewal initiatives.
  • Track portfolio performance and ensure timely escalation of material commercial or retention risks.
  • Develop clear communications and performance updates for relevant stakeholders.

2. New Business and Network Growth

  • Support the regional New Store Sales agenda by identifying and developing network-led growth opportunities.
  • Work with Area, regional, and global commercial teams to improve cross-regional selling and opportunity conversion.
  • Develop structured customer and market opportunity pipelines.
  • Enable commercial teams with relevant product propositions, customer insights, capability material, and value cases.
  • Support the development of scalable network-selling models and repeatable commercial plays.
  • Track opportunity progress, conversion performance, and barriers requiring regional intervention.

3. Customer Profitability and Value Creation

  • Conduct customer-level revenue, gross profit, cost-to-serve, and profitability analysis.
  • Identify financial leakage, margin risks, and structural performance gaps.
  • Facilitate regular customer profitability discussions with commercial, customer experience, operations, and finance teams.
  • Develop and drive corrective actions for underperforming accounts.
  • Identify opportunities for upselling, value-added services, scope expansion, and product penetration.
  • Partner with Customer Program Managers, Lead Customer Managers, sales teams, and network stakeholders to convert identified opportunities.
  • Lead or support value-generation initiatives across the customer portfolio.
  • Establish mechanisms to measure the financial and customer impact of value-creation initiatives.

4. Financial Performance Management

  • Support the regional financial management and governance of the Lead Logistics portfolio.
  • Monitor revenue, gross profit, margins, cost performance, and other relevant financial health indicators.
  • Partner with Finance to improve transparency, accuracy, and accountability in customer and product financial performance.
  • Support monthly performance management and forecasting processes.
  • Identify material financial variances and ensure that root causes and recovery actions are clearly defined.
  • Drive improvements in financial hygiene, data quality, and performance reporting.
  • Support the development of business cases for growth, transformation, and capability investments.

5. Operational and Product Performance

  • Support the transformation and continuous improvement of operational capabilities, including consolidation operations.
  • Partner with Operations and Procurement to improve service quality, productivity, supplier performance, and cost competitiveness.
  • Identify systemic operational issues and drive structured root-cause resolution.
  • Support the development and implementation of consistent operating standards and ways of working.
  • Contribute to product-market fit assessments, service-model design, and operational scalability.
  • Monitor productivity and operational performance metrics and coordinate improvement interventions.
  • Ensure operational initiatives are aligned with customer requirements and product strategy.

6. Product Capabilities and Systems Adoption

  • Drive adoption and effective utilisation of Lead Logistics platforms, systems, and digital capabilities.
  • Act as a regional focal point for selected technology platforms, product applications, or user communities.
  • Partner with global and regional technology teams to translate business requirements into capability improvements.
  • Support user engagement, implementation, change management, and adoption tracking.
  • Identify capability gaps and coordinate improvement priorities.
  • Develop regional product and systems expertise through structured knowledge sharing and capability-building activities.
  • Promote standardization and reduce reliance on local or manual solutions where scalable product capabilities are available.

7. Strategic Projects and Product Initiatives

  • Lead or support regional and global product projects, transformation programs, and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Represent the region in Center led product-development and capability programs.
  • Translate global product priorities into regional execution plans.
  • Establish clear project scope, milestones, governance, ownership, risks, and success measures.
  • Coordinate stakeholders across functions and geographies to ensure timely delivery.
  • Develop recommendations, business cases, and decision material for senior leadership.
  • Track delivery, benefits realization, and sustainability of implemented solutions.

8. Customer and Product Advocacy

  • Support programs that strengthen senior product engagement with strategic customers.
  • Facilitate product leadership participation in key customer interactions, business reviews, and strategic discussions.
  • Capture customer feedback and convert it into product, service, and capability improvements.
  • Promote customer-centric decision-making across product and operational teams.
  • Strengthen the connection between customer requirements, commercial propositions, and product-development priorities.

9. Capability Building and Communication

  • Develop product playbooks, training material, capability guides, customer propositions, and operational reference material.
  • Build product capability across commercial, customer experience, and operational teams.
  • Coordinate regional newsletters, product updates, success stories, and knowledge-sharing forums.
  • Create clear executive-level communications on performance, priorities, risks, and initiatives.
  • Support the development of a strong regional product-management community.
  • Promote consistent understanding of the Lead Logistics value proposition and product capabilities.

Key Stakeholders

The role will work closely with:

  • Regional and Area Product Management teams
  • Sales and Business Development teams
  • Local/Global Customer Account Managers and Program Managers
  • Customer Experience and Operations teams
  • Finance and Business Performance teams
  • Procurement and supplier-management teams
  • Technology, platform, and implementation teams
  • Global and Centre Product teams
  • Regional and Area leadership
  • Strategic customers and external partners

Decision-Making and Accountability

The Product Manager will be expected to:

  • Take ownership of assigned portfolio priorities and initiatives.
  • Provide fact-based recommendations to senior stakeholders.
  • Challenge performance gaps and drive clear corrective actions.
  • Escalate material customer, financial, operational, or delivery risks.
  • Balance regional requirements with global product standards.
  • Influence decisions across teams without relying on formal reporting lines.
  • Ensure initiatives deliver measurable commercial, financial, operational, or customer outcomes.

Capabilities

  • Strategic and commercial acumen with the ability to translate business priorities into growth, retention, profitability, and value-creation initiatives.
  • Strong customer, supply chain, and market understanding, including customer operating models, logistics solutions, and industry dynamics.
  • Financial and analytical capability to assess customer P&L, identify performance gaps, and develop fact-based recommendations.
  • Commercial solution-selling understanding, including opportunity development, value articulation, upselling, and cross-functional pursuit management.
  • Digital and technology understanding, with the ability to support platform adoption, capability development, and technology-enabled transformation.
  • Stakeholder management and influencing skills to drive outcomes across commercial, customer experience, operations, finance, procurement, and technology teams.
  • Programme and change-management capability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives from concept through implementation and benefits realisation.
  • Clear executive communication skills, including the ability to simplify complex issues and present compelling recommendations.

Who We Are Looking For

We are looking for a mature, commercially minded and analytically strong product-management professional who can operate effectively & independently in a complex, matrixed organization. The ideal candidate will:

  • Be customer focused, outcome oriented, and comfortable taking end-to-end ownership.
  • Combine strategic thinking with disciplined execution.
  • Use data and financial insight to identify opportunities and challenge underperformance.
  • Influence senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority.
  • Navigate ambiguity, prioritise competing demands, and maintain momentum.
  • Connect commercial, operational, financial, and technology perspectives.
  • Drive standardisation, scalability, and continuous improvement.
  • Communicate with clarity, credibility, and confidence across functions and levels.

Performance Measures

Specific

  • Customer Retention opportunity P&L
  • SSS Pipeline Win %, Churn %
  • Profitable Growth & P&L Delivery
  • Project-based outcome delivery

Shared

  • Operational & Financial Health Metrics
  • Customer satisfaction

title: Sr. Refrigeration Controls Engineer
description:
ARE YOU A CURRENT US FOODS EMPLOYEE? PLEASE APPLY DIRECTLY THROUGH OUR INTERNAL WORKDAY CAREER SITE

Join Our Community of Food People!

The Senior Refrigeration Controls Engineer is responsible for the design, programming, optimization, and support of refrigeration control systems across food distribution and cold storage facilities. This role ensures safe, reliable, and energy-efficient operation of temperature-controlled environments supporting perishable food logistics. The position provides technical leadership in controls architecture, automation strategy, troubleshooting, and system standardization across multiple sites.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Refrigeration Controls & Automation

  • Lead the design, programming, commissioning, troubleshooting, and optimization of industrial refrigeration control systems.

  • Support controls infrastructure for ammonia (NH3) and Freon refrigeration systems including compressors, condensers, evaporators, vessels, pumps, valves, and defrost systems.

  • Develop and maintain PLC, HMI, SCADA, and building automation system (BAS) control strategies for refrigeration operations.

  • Monitor and optimize refrigeration system performance, energy efficiency, alarm management, and temperature compliance.

  • Troubleshoot complex refrigeration controls, instrumentation, and automation failures impacting facility operations and product integrity.

Operational Reliability & Compliance

  • Ensure refrigeration systems operate safely and in compliance with OSHA PSM, EPA RMP, IIAR, and applicable food safety regulations.

  • Support process hazard analysis (PHA), management of change (MOC), and refrigeration safety management programs.

  • Lead root cause analysis of investigations for refrigeration system failures, operational incidents, and recurring equipment issues.

  • Support emergency response planning and operational readiness for refrigeration-related incidents.

    • PLC Experience- Rockwell, Allen Bradley Siemens.​

    • SCADA/Network Controls

Controls Systems & OT Infrastructure

  • Support industrial control system architecture including PLCs, HMIs, SCADA systems, VFDs, instrumentation, and industrial networking.

  • Manage integration between refrigeration systems, facility monitoring systems, warehouse automation systems, and enterprise platforms.

  • Support industrial communication protocols including Ethernet/IP, Modbus, BACnet, and OPC.

  • Partner with IT and cybersecurity teams to maintain secure and reliable OT environments.

Capital Projects & System Improvements

  • Lead refrigeration controls engineering activities for capital projects, facility expansions, retrofits, and modernization initiatives.

  • Develop technical specifications, control narratives, sequence of operations, and commissioning plans.

  • Coordinate activities with refrigeration contractors, OEMs, system integrators, and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Support startup, commissioning, and operational handoff of new refrigeration and automation systems.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve refrigeration system reliability, uptime, energy usage, and operational efficiency.

  • Utilize operational data and analytics to support predictive maintenance and system optimization strategies.

  • Standardize refrigeration controls architecture, engineering documentation, and best practices across facilities.

  • Mentor junior engineers, technicians, and maintenance personnel on refrigeration controls systems and troubleshooting methodologies.

  • Other duties as assigned by manager.

RELATIONSHIPS

  • Internal Relationships: This role partners closely with Operations, Facilities, Maintenance, EHS, Asset Management, and Engineers.

  • External Relationships: Interfaces with external engineering firms, refrigeration contractors, equipment suppliers, third party contractors, and consultants.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Travel to multiple distribution centers as needed.

  • Combination of office, warehouse, and field environments, including refrigerated and frozen areas.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5 years of experience supporting industrial refrigeration and controls systems in food distribution, cold storage, food manufacturing, or industrial operations.

  • Direct experience with ammonia refrigeration systems.

  • Experience in highly automated, temperature-controlled, or 24/7 operational environments.

  • Strong knowledge of Process Safety Management (PSM) and Risk Management Program (RMP) compliance requirements.

  • Demonstrated experience in system troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and operational problem-solving within industrial refrigeration environments.

  • Experience supporting capital projects, including system upgrades, expansions, commissioning, and equipment optimization initiatives.

  • Proficient in interpreting and developing P&IDs, technical specifications, and engineering documentation.

  • Strong understanding of asset reliability, preventative maintenance strategies, and energy optimization practices.

  • Familiarity with OSHA and EPA requirements.

  • PLC/Automation experience in Rockwell, Siemen, Allen Bradley as well as SCADA and HMI interfaces.

  • This role requires approximately >25% travel during the initial years, with the potential for reduced travel as the function matures and stabilizes.

EDUCATION

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical/Mechanical Engineering or related technical discipline

CERTIFICATIONS/TRAINING

  • Certified Controls Engineer (CCE)​

  • Certified Automation Prof. (CAP) or CCST

LICENSES

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Certified Automation Engineer with combination of experience

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience supporting Freon, C02 and or Ammonia refrigeration systems.

  • Experience in food distribution, cold storage, manufacturing, or logistics environments.

  • Experience supporting multi-site operations.

PHYSICAL QUALIFICATIONS

  • Standard required physical activities including length of time performing each activity.

This role will also receive annual incentive plan bonus.​

To review available benefits, please click here: https://www.usfoods.com/careers/benefits.html.

$110,000 - $175,000

title: Data Scientist | Financial Crime | Transaction Monitoring @ING Hubs Romania
description:
Discover ING Hubs Romania

ING Hubs Romania offers 130 services in software development, data management, non-financial risk & compliance, audit, and retail operations to 24 ING units worldwide, with the help of over 2000 high-performing engineers, risk, and operations professionals.

We started out in 2015 as ING’s software development hub, then steadily expanded our range to include more services and competencies. Now we provide borderless services with bank-wide capabilities and operate from our office in Bucharest.

Our tech capabilities remain the core of our business, with more than 1800 colleagues active in Data Management, Touchpoint Channels & Integration, Core Banking, and Global Products.

We enjoy a flexible way of working and a highly collaborative environment, where fair and constructive feedback is encouraged.

For us, impact isn't a perk. It's the driver of our work. We are guided and rewarded by a shared desire to make the world a better place, one innovative solution at a time. Our colleagues make it their job to do impactful things and they love doing it in good company. Do you?

The Mission
Within ING, there is ING Analytics (INGA) - a major driving force in its digital transformation of the bank. By creating measurable value for ING and its customers through world-class analytics products and services, INGA helps ING to become a data-driven leader. Among others, INGA delivers call & speech analytics, generative AI in risk summarization, insights into portfolio performance, advanced ESG data insights (commercial purposes), data analytics platforms (cloud and on-premises), and many more.

We are looking for a Data Scientist to join us in Bucharest. In this role, you will be responsible for scoping, developing, validating, and documenting machine-learning-based solutions which will form the core of the products that INGA develops. You will collaborate closely with other scientists and analysts in evaluating model performance to ensure the best possible performance.

Your day-to-day

A typical day for a data scientist starts with coffee, catching up with colleagues, and drafting a plan for the coming day. After the standup, you will start developing machine learning solutions, adopting best practices and quality standards for fit-for-purpose model pipelines. As an effective team member of the model development & implementation team, you will challenge the status quo while addressing the requirements of the ING model governance.

After lunch, you will prepare fraud advance models to be deployed to production. Finally, to wrap up the day, you will actively explore INGA’s domain and engage in creating a journey that makes our bank and our society safer.

What you’ll bring to the team

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, mathematics, engineering, or econometrics.

  • 1-3 years of work experience in the data science field.

  • Good understanding of supervised and unsupervised machine learning methods.

  • Strong Python programming skills, Apache Spark, SQL, Git.

  • Excellent communication skills, capable of working collaboratively in a semi-remote, globally distributed team.

Nice to have

  • Broad experience with end-to-end machine learning projects; involvement in all modeling steps (from data extraction to production).

  • Background in writing production-ready code and a solid understanding of object-oriented programming is a strong plus.

  • Proactive and can-do attitude (self-steering).

  • Curious mindset; you are collaborative and passionate about helping others to grow and improve.

  • Able to embrace challenges in a fast-changing and complex environment.

title: Pharmacy Intern
description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
  • Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
  • Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
  • Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

  • Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
  • Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
  • Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
  • Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Required Qualifications:

  • Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy
  • Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Essential Functions:

  • Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
  • Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
  • Attention and Focus:
    • Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time
    • Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs
    • Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
  • Customer Service and Team Orientation:
    • Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner
    • Notice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
  • Communication Skills:
    • Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleagues
    • Utilize active listening by giving full attention to what others are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times
  • Mathematical Reasoning:
    • Ability to use math to solve a problem, such as determining the total number of tablets to dispense, day’s supply, and/or number of full bottles and additional bottles needed to fill a prescription
  • Problem Resolution:
    • Identifying challenging patient or colleague interactions and choosing the best course of action when faced multiple options
  • Physical Demands:
    • Be mobile and remain upright for extended periods of time
    • Lift, scan, and bag items
    • Reach overhead; stretch or reach out with the body, arms, and/or legs to grasp items
    • Move fingers repetitively; picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than whole hand or arm
    • Extend hand(s) and arm(s) multiple directions to place, move, or lift items
    • Control precision; quickly adjust machines to exact positions
    • Stoop to a considerable degree, requiring full use of the lower extremities and back muscles to move items between low and high positions, including bending spine at the waist
    • Close visual acuity to perform activities such as: transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, reading, visual inspection involving small parts
    • Occasionally lift of up to 20 lbs and/or exert up to 20 lbs. of force; Frequently lift of up to 10 lbs and/or exert up to 10 lbs. of force; Consistently lift and/or exert a negligible amount of force to move objects.
    • Express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word where detailed or important spoken instructions must be conveyed accurately
    • ; Have the ability to receive detailed information through oral communication
  • Any additional tasks as directed by Supervisor or Manager

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of related work experience in pharmacy, retail, medical, or customer service setting
  • Ability to become immunization certified: Once state regulations are met, pharmacy interns should be striving to provide patient immunizations as this is an essential pharmacist function
  • Ability to work in home store, and across the market in other locations, to meet business needs
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.)

Pay Range

The typical pay range for this role is:


$18.00 - $19.75


Whether in our pharmacies or through our health service offerings, we are pioneering a bold new approach to total health care. As health care innovators, we are making quality care affordable, accessible, simple and seamless. We await your fresh ideas, new perspectives, and the unique contributions you will make to our organization.

Great benefits for great people

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

This part‑time position is eligible for a range of benefits and programs that support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues. Depending on hours worked and eligibility, the benefits for this position include dental, vision, wellness resources, employee discounts, access to certain voluntary benefits, and other programs.

title: Business Analyst II
description:
Site: Mass General Brigham Incorporated


Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.


Job Summary

About the Role
The Mass General Physicians Organization Business Intelligence Team is seeking a collaborative Business Analyst to help teams access, understand, and use data to support operational decision-making. In this role, you will partner with stakeholders, translate business needs into clear reporting requirements, support reporting tools and workflows, and help ensure data and reports are accurate, reliable, and easy to use.

What You’ll Do
• Partner with stakeholders to gather, evaluate, document, and prioritize data and reporting requests.
• Serve as a key point of contact for business intelligence requests, including intake, clarification, coordination, and follow-up.
• Respond promptly to high-priority tickets and customer requests, clarifying needs and providing guidance to ensure the final information addresses the issue.
• Translate business rules, workflows, and operational needs into clear reporting requirements and specifications for developers.
• Coordinate project queues and support resource planning, including assigning and tracking work through Workfront.
• Support the full reporting lifecycle, including requirements gathering, planning, development validation, testing, rollout, training, and production support.
• Validate reporting solutions before production release to ensure they meet user requirements and quality expectations.
• Collaborate with Operations, IT, vendors, customers, leadership, and business users to deliver reliable and useful information.
• Use knowledge of existing reports in IPORT, Epic, and other reporting tools to determine whether a new request can be met with an existing solution.
• Develop an understanding of Revenue Cycle data and related business processes to serve as a subject matter resource for reporting needs.
• Create documentation, process flows, best-practice scenarios, training materials, and specifications that support reporting and analytics work.
• Assist with end-user training and cross-train peers in relevant subject matter and technical areas.
• Contribute to project plans, establish baseline and target metrics, and participate in process improvement efforts across Finance IS, MGPO Finance, MGH, and MGB as needed.
• May lead cross-functional teams to address business or systems issues.


Qualifications

What You’ll Bring

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and collaboration skills.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to gather requirements, explain findings, and deliver presentations.
  • Experience gathering business requirements and translating them into actionable reporting or analytics specifications.
  • Ability to work effectively with business users, technical teams, vendors, operations partners, and leadership.
  • Experience creating and executing test cases to support accurate, high-quality reporting.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • A proactive, process-driven approach with a strong focus on understanding and exceeding customer needs.
  • Ability to build productive relationships with peers, supervisors, customers, and management.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Two to four years of experience in a business intelligence, data warehouse, data mart, OLAP, or operational reporting environment.
  • Knowledge of relational and dimensional data models.
  • Knowledge of structured query language (SQL).
  • Understanding of Lean Six Sigma concepts and continuous improvement principles.
  • Understanding of basic financial and business principles in a healthcare setting.
  • Experience working with Epic, IPORT, Revenue Cycle data, or healthcare reporting tools.

How You’ll Succeed

  • You are curious about how data supports business operations and enjoy turning complex questions into clear requirements.
  • You communicate well with both technical and non-technical partners and can tailor your message to different audiences.
  • You are organized, responsive, and comfortable balancing multiple requests and priorities.
  • You take ownership of follow-through and help ensure reporting solutions are accurate, useful, and aligned with stakeholder needs.
  • You enjoy documenting processes, sharing knowledge, and supporting end users as they adopt tools and reports.

  • M-F Eastern business hours required

title: Legal Practice Specialist, Texas
description:
About the role

The Legal Practice Specialist, Texas serves as a Texas litigation-practice subject-matter resource across sales, product, operations and customer support. The role is designed for an experienced Texas litigation paralegal or legal assistant moving into legal technology, and sits at the intersection of sales, marketing, product, and operations, reporting to the Chief Operating Officer. The incumbent trains and supports the sales team, serves as the voice of the Texas customer in product and workflow development, grounds new products (including AI-powered tools) in real-world practice, liaises with courts on procedural requirements, and provides practitioner and market insight to support leadership's growth planning in Texas.
This is not a fee-earning role and does not involve providing legal advice to customers or the public.

Compensation:The salary range for this exempt position is $85,000–$100,000 annually. The final offer will be determined based on the candidate’s experience, education, qualifications, internal equity, and the company’s compensation philosophy.

About InfoTrack

InfoTrack is a platform that seamlessly connects law firms to the courts and to the services that they need to litigate successfully. We're global leaders in legal technology with unparalleled expertise in forging integrations that can drastically improve the efficiency of law firms and the legal system.

As a highly ambitious company, we know that our people are critical to our success. That's why we're passionate about fostering a high-performance culture built on professional development, open communication, and transparent leadership. If you're smart, dedicated, and eager to help build a market-leading solution that makes a difference in the lives of our clients, join us.

Responsibilities

  • Sales and Account Enablement
    • Create and deliver Texas practice training for the sales team, including onboarding curriculum and recurring clinics.
    • Join sales calls and product demos as the resident practice expert; maintain an objection and FAQ library.
    • Partner with sales and account management on major account reviews, diagnosing practice-level issues and workshopping solutions.
  • Product and Voice of the Customer
    • Represent the Texas customer in product and operations workflow development.
    • Serve as subject matter expert and contributes Texas practice knowledge to the evaluation and development of new products and features., including AI-powered tools.
    • Perform user acceptance testing on new releases and document findings.
  • Courts and Local Knowledge
    • Liaise with court clerks, contacting courts to clarify filing and procedural requirements on InfoTrack’s behalf.
    • Maintain internal knowledge of county-level requirements, local rule changes, and clerk practice shifts.
  • Marketing and Community
    • Fact-check marketing and customer support materials on Texas practice.
    • Identify local marketing opportunities: conferences, events, and partnerships with bar, paralegal, and trial lawyer associations.
    • Contribute practitioner content such as webinars, best-practice guides, and help center articles.
  • Customer Education and Support
    • Act as an escalation resource for customer support on Texas practice questions.
    • Help develop customer-facing education and training materials.
  • Strategy
    • Partner with strategic leaders to workshop plans and objectives for growth in Texas.
    • Bring practitioner and market intelligence into strategic planning.

Requirements

  • Four (4) or more years of hands-on experience as a litigation paralegal or legal assistant in Texas civil litigation. Plaintiff-side experience, such as personal injury or consumer law, strongly preferred.
  • Hands-on eFiling experience across multiple Texas counties through eFileTexas, including familiarity with county-level differences in clerk review, rejection reasons, and citation issuance.
  • Direct experience coordinating service of process, including engaging certified process servers, tracking attempts, reviewing affidavits and returns, and supporting motions for substituted service.
  • Hands-on experience tracking Texas dockets, deadlines, and case status across courts. Experience across more than one Texas metro area preferred.
  • Deep working knowledge of Texas trial court structure, clerk practices, and mandatory eFiling mechanics at the county level.
  • Strong knowledge of Texas service of process rules and practice, including manner of service, diligence documentation, affidavits, and proof-of-service instruments.
  • Demonstrated ability to teach: has trained colleagues, written training guides or internal procedure documentation, and can explain a procedure clearly to a non-lawyer.
  • Comfort with legal software beyond routine use, including aptitude for evaluating new systems, testing releases, and reporting reproducible findings.
  • Ability to work effectively across functions and in ambiguous environments, translating firm-side practice knowledge into product, marketing, and strategic recommendations.
  • Active involvement in professional associations (paralegal, bar, or trial lawyer organizations), including contributing to initiatives, trainings, or events; preferred.
  • Must reside in the United States


    Certifications:
    Paralegal certification (for example, Texas Board of Legal Specialization or NALA Certified Paralegal) preferred.

Benefits

What sets InfoTrack apartWe strive to ensure that you have the resources and training that you need to successfully collaborate and succeed. At InfoTrack, we’re committed to a workplace where everyone feels comfortable to do their best work and, yes, have fun!


We offer:

Excellent health, dental, and vision plans, 401k match, 20 days of paid time off, plus more competitive benefits.

Work with a knowledgeable, high-achieving, experienced, and fun team.

Be part of a culture obsessive about learning, development, and career growth.

Learn more about life at InfoTrack on our website.


InfoTrack is certified as a Great Place to Work®

title: Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) - Golden, CO
description:
Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) $62K-80K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Starting Salary range: $62,000.00 - $80,000.00 per year.
  • 401K with maximum employee matching.
  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

We will rely on your expertise to:

  • Evaluate mental health conditions, diagnose, create, and implement a treatment plan, complete ongoing documentation including further diagnosis, treatment plan reviews, and case notes according to company policy.
  • Provide excellent care for clients and collaborate with a dynamic team to further the mission of filling gaps in our community.
  • Utilize creativity in interventions to help clients achieve and exceed goals.
  • Prepare and submit individual documentation for each session per company guidelines and protocol.
  • For Full-Time status, clinicians must maintain at least 32 available hours for patient care per week.
  • Coordinate services with other care providers, families, work personnel, medical personnel, other OptiMindHealth staff, and school staff as needed.
  • Attend and participate in all clinical staff meetings and trainings.

Qualifications and Skill for This Positions:

  • Master's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college/university.
  • Full, current, unrestricted license to practice independently (LPC, LCSW, LMFT) is required.
  • Experience with electronic health records and completing clinical documentation.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience and willingness to work collaboratively and creatively to meet necessary deadlines.
  • Comfort and familiarity working with clients with a diverse range of problems or concerns.
  • Ability to pass a background check in a way that confirms to us you can provide safe care.
  • Demonstrate and model stable and appropriate boundaries with clients.

Additionally Valuable (but not essential) Qualifications for This Position:

  • Experience working in community, group, or private practice mental health.
  • Currently paneled or credentialed with insurance network.
  • Multilingual or bilingual proficiency.
  • Specialty area of practice.

We can’t wait to hear your story and look forward to sharing ours!

They represent typical elements and criteria considered necessary to perform the job successfully. The job’s responsibilities/tasks may be modified and/or expanded over time. OMH will inform the employee when changes in the respective job description are made.

Salary: $62,000 – $80,000 / year

title: INTERNSHIP - Corporate Sector Coverage and Real Estate
description:
ING Luxembourg is looking for a Corporate Sector Coverage and Real Estate Intern to strengthen its Wholesale Banking department for a 6-month internship (or longer), starting in November 2026.

Please note that only students who can provide a valid internship agreement (school convention) will be considered.

About the department:

As part of ING Wholesale Banking, the Corporate Sector Coverage team serves large local and multinational companies in Luxembourg, managing approximately 150 clients through a multi-product, multi-location strategy and focusing on long-term relationships. Within the Real Estate segment, the team supports Real Estate investment funds and key Real Estate players (e.g. Private Equity Sponsors, Insurers, SWFs, Developers etc.) involved in high-profile financing transactions in Luxembourg, spanning both asset-based lending and unsecured fund financing to investment grade REITs and private capital structures on a pan European level. The facilities and products provided to our clients are varied in structure and complexity, which requires an adequate professional level of client coverage and product knowledge.

Your main tasks will be to:

Prepare client pitches, assist with business committee submissions, market analysis, support the Relationship Managers on their workflow pertaining to deal structuring, KYC and Client Due Diligence matters in the context of account opening and entity onboarding, different projects arising on an ad hoc basis and generally support the Relationship Managers in their day-to-day work.

Your profile:

  • Preference for candidates in their final year of study, with a strong academic track record
  • Prior experience through internships is of added value but not pre-requisite
  • Detail-oriented team-player with strong analytical skills
  • Excellent English verbal and written communication skills are required, any other additional languages are a plus
  • Looking for candidates with a strong eagerness to learn and who thrive in fast-paced environments

Your working environment:

With over 900 employees in the Grand Duchy and thanks to the combination of our local presence and the strength of a robust multinational like ING, we offer our business customers a wide range of solutions through the channel of their choice.

ING is a global bank with a strong European base. 53,000 employees serve around 38.4 million customers, corporate clients, and financial institutions in over 40 countries. Operating in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg since 1960 as a universal and accessible bank, our products include savings, payments, investments, loans and mortgages for private banking customers, whom we sever serve online and through our network of branches. For our Wholesale Banking clients, we provide lending, sustainable finance, payment & cash management and fund services.

title: Chief Steward
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Manages the daily kitchen utility operations and staff. Areas of responsibilities include dish room operations, night cleaning, back dock cleaning and maintenance, banquet plating and food running. Supervises kitchen employees not actively engaged in cooking (e.g., dishwashers, kitchen helpers, etc.). Strives to continually improve guest and employee satisfaction while maintaining the operating budget.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or GED; 4 years experience in the procurement, food and beverage, culinary, or related professional area.

OR

• 2-year degree in Hotel and Restaurant Management, Hospitality, Business Administration, or related major; 2 years experience in the procurement, food and beverage, culinary, or related professional area.

Managing Day-to-Day Operations

• Orders and manages necessary supplies. Ensuring workers have supplies, equipment, tools, and uniforms necessary to do their jobs.

• Schedules events, programs, and activities, as well as the work of others.

• Monitors the inflow of ordered materials and the maintenance of current materials.

• Conducts china, glass and silver inventories.

• Enforces proper cleaning routines for serviceware, equipment, floors, etc.

• Ensures compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.

• Ensures compliance with food handling and sanitation standards.

• Informs and/or updates the executives, the peers and the subordinates on relevant information in a timely manner.

• Encourages and builds mutual trust, respect, and cooperation among team members.

• Communicates performance expectations in accordance with job descriptions for each position.

• Establishes and maintains open, collaborative relationships with employees.

• Participates in the management of department's controllable expenses to achieve or exceed budgeted goals.

• Strives to improve service performance.

• Solicits employee feedback.

• Understands the impact of department's operation on the overall property financial goals and objectives.

Ensuring Exceptional Customer Service

• Attends meetings and communicates with executive, peers, and subordinates as an effort to improve quality of service.

• Manages day-to-day operations, ensures the quality, standards and meeting the expectations of the customers on a daily basis.

• Emphasizes guest satisfaction during all departmental meetings and focuses on continuous improvement.

Managing and Conducting Human Resource Activities

• Recruits, interviews, selects, hires, and promotes employees in the organization.

• Trains employees in safety procedures.

• Ensures utility staff is properly trained regarding sanitation, equipment handling and chemical usage.

title: Pharmacy Intern
description:
You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.

Position Summary:

At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.

As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.

3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:

  • Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
  • Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
  • Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
  • Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
  • Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
  • Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
  • Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
  • Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
  • Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
  • Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
  • Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification

Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:

  • Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
  • Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
  • Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
  • Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Required Qualifications:

  • Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy
  • Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required

Essential Functions:

  • Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
  • Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
  • Attention and Focus:
    • Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time
    • Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs
    • Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
  • Customer Service and Team Orientation:
    • Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner
    • Notice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
  • Communication Skills:
    • Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleagues
    • Utilize active listening by giving full attention to what others are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times
  • Mathematical Reasoning:
    • Ability to use math to solve a problem, such as determining the total number of tablets to dispense, day’s supply, and/or number of full bottles and additional bottles needed to fill a prescription
  • Problem Resolution:
    • Identifying challenging patient or colleague interactions and choosing the best course of action when faced multiple options
  • Physical Demands:
    • Be mobile and remain upright for extended periods of time
    • Lift, scan, and bag items
    • Reach overhead; stretch or reach out with the body, arms, and/or legs to grasp items
    • Move fingers repetitively; picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than whole hand or arm
    • Extend hand(s) and arm(s) multiple directions to place, move, or lift items
    • Control precision; quickly adjust machines to exact positions
    • Stoop to a considerable degree, requiring full use of the lower extremities and back muscles to move items between low and high positions, including bending spine at the waist
    • Close visual acuity to perform activities such as: transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, reading, visual inspection involving small parts
    • Occasionally lift of up to 20 lbs and/or exert up to 20 lbs. of force; Frequently lift of up to 10 lbs and/or exert up to 10 lbs. of force; Consistently lift and/or exert a negligible amount of force to move objects.
    • Express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word where detailed or important spoken instructions must be conveyed accurately
    • Have the ability to receive detailed information through oral communication
  • Any additional tasks as directed by Supervisor or Manager

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of related work experience in pharmacy, retail, medical, or customer service setting
  • Ability to become immunization certified: Once state regulations are met, pharmacy interns should be striving to provide patient immunizations as this is an essential pharmacist function
  • Ability to work in home store, and across the market in other locations, to meet business needs
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.)

Pay Range

The typical pay range for this role is:


$20.00 - $23.75


Whether in our pharmacies or through our health service offerings, we are pioneering a bold new approach to total health care. As health care innovators, we are making quality care affordable, accessible, simple and seamless. We await your fresh ideas, new perspectives, and the unique contributions you will make to our organization.

Great benefits for great people

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

This part‑time position is eligible for a range of benefits and programs that support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues. Depending on hours worked and eligibility, the benefits for this position include dental, vision, wellness resources, employee discounts, access to certain voluntary benefits, and other programs.

title: PWM Risk, Vice President
location: Purchase, New York, United States of America
description:
Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, investment management and wealth management services. The Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments and individuals from more than 1,200 offices in 43 countries. Private Wealth Management (PWM) is the boutique business within Morgan Stanley Wealth Management that is exclusively focused on the ultra-high net worth (UHNW) client segment.


As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people is critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in integrity, excellence and strong team ethic. As a Facilities Technician, you will play a key role in supporting the day-to-day operation and maintenance of site facilities, utilities, and building systems. You will help maintain accurate maintenance records within the CMMS system, support equipment calibration and qualification activities, and ensure preventative maintenance schedules remain up to date. In addition, you will assist with contractor management, site access administration, and maintaining compliance with health, safety, and GMP requirements, helping to ensure a safe and well-maintained working environment.

Main responsibilities will include:

  • Support safe working practices by ensuring contractors follow site health & safety and GMP requirements.

  • Participate in site improvement projects, working alongside engineers, technicians, and other departments.

  • Provide support during facility and manufacturing area checks, qualifications, and validations as required.

  • Assist with managing site access badges, including issuing replacements and supporting day‑to‑day access needs.

  • Assist with maintaining maintenance records and equipment information within the CMMS system.

  • Help keep preventative maintenance and calibration schedules up to date when new equipment is installed or existing equipment is changed.

About you

  • You have a basic understanding of mechanical, electrical, or building systems and are eager to develop your technical knowledge.

  • You hold a trade qualification or have a technical background, which would be a strong advantage.

  • You have 1–2 years of experience in facilities, maintenance, technical support, or a similar hands-on environment.

  • You possess good computer skills and can accurately complete maintenance records, reports, and checklists.

  • You can prioritise tasks, manage competing demands, and know when to escalate issues or seek support.

title: Materials Inventory Assistant
location: Paranaque City, National Capital Region (Manila), Philippines
description:

With over 30 years of experience in semiconductor innovation, we bring that purpose to life across every part of the business—from breakthrough product development and customer success to how we show up for each other and the communities we serve.

The Opportunity

Allegro is looking for a meticulous and proactive Materials Management Specialist to join our dynamic team, playing a pivotal role in ensuring the efficient and accurate flow of materials that power our production. In this position, you will be at the heart of our inventory operations, from precise issuance and receipt management to optimizing storage and coordinating with various internal and external partners. This is an exceptional opportunity for someone who thrives on accuracy, enjoys problem-solving, and is committed to continuous improvement within a fast-paced manufacturing environment. If you are detail-oriented, have a strong understanding of inventory principles, and are eager to contribute to operational excellence, you will find significant growth and impact here at Allegro.


What You Will Do

  • Ensure Accurate Issuance & Transactions: Manage the issuance of direct and indirect materials based on production requirements, ensuring all requests are fulfilled and accurately encoded in Oracle within the shift. Verify the correctness of quantities and part numbers against Move Orders and reconcile any discrepancies.
  • Optimize Inventory Management: Implement and monitor the "First In, First Out" (FIFO) method for material issuance and arrangement. Conduct daily cycle counts of precious metals and weekly cycle counts of all direct and indirect materials.
  • Manage Material Flow & Storage: Oversee the proper handling and storage of all materials and spare parts. Coordinate thawing of molding compounds and manage the replenishment and availability of materials in production stores and cold storages.
  • Support Production & Quality: Expedite urgent materials under IQC evaluation and coordinate with Assembly/Test Process Engineering for new material qualifications. Monitor expiration dates and manage NCR/Waiver processes for affected material lots.
  • Handle Returns & Repairs: Process returned reject materials from production and worn-out spare parts, ensuring proper surrender and replacement procedures. Monitor the status of items sent for repair and follow up with relevant teams.
  • Maintain Data Integrity & Reporting: Accurately transact all withdrawals in Oracle, ensuring correct entry of issued inventory materials and lot numbers. Generate monthly spare parts Oracle reports and other relevant reports for analysis and discrepancy resolution.
  • Operate Material Handling Equipment: Safely operate Forklift/Reach Truck, Foton Van, and Shuttle Car for material retrieval and transfer to staging areas.
  • Drive Continuous Improvement: Identify and recommend systems and policies to enhance department services, effectiveness, and efficiency. Ensure the implementation of "5S" principles in all storage areas and individual workspaces.
  • Ensure Security & Compliance: Be responsible for the security of all material storage areas. Ensure Oracle system locators align with actual stock locations.

What Will You Bring?

  • A College Graduate qualification.
  • At least 2 years of work experience in handling inventory and warehousing within a manufacturing company.
  • Proficiency in computer software and the Oracle System.
  • Knowledge and ability to operate/drive a forklift and Van (with a professional Driver’s license).
  • Capability to diligently satisfy end-user requirements and priorities.
  • Demonstrated teamwork and strong knowledge in Materials Management.

Why Allegro?

Join Allegro and become part of a team where your contributions truly matter.

We foster a culture of Real Innovation, empowering you to push boundaries, develop cutting-edge solutions, and drive continuous improvement.
Your work will create a Real Impact by solving complex real-world challenges that fuel our success and shape the future of technology.
You’ll experience Real Connection, collaborating with talented colleagues around the globe in an environment built on trust, respect, and a shared purpose.
Join us—and help build what’s next.

title: Intern, Debt Capital Markets APAC
description:
Why ING?

The world of banking is changing faster than ever. That’s why we at ING are always broadening our horizons. Our people have a forward-thinking mentality, a strong can-do spirit and enjoy working in an agile environment.

ING in Asia Pacific

In Asia Pacific, ING offers wholesale banking across 11 markets, namely Australia, China, Hong Kong SAR, India, Indonesia, Japan, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, and Vietnam.

ING offers both retail and wholesale banking services in Australia. ING’s regional presence includes a 13% stake in Bank of Beijing, China and a 30% stake in TMBThanachart Bank in Thailand.

Singapore is the regional headquarters for ING's Wholesale Banking (WB) business in Asia, which includes all WB business lines such as Financial Markets, Strategic Products, Sectors, Lending and Transaction Services and other support functions.

What does the Debt Capital Markets Team do in ING?

Debt Capital Markets team assists our APAC clients in structuring and raising debt financing through various bond instruments, across both investment grade and high yield bonds. We provide access for sovereign, corporate and financial institution bond issuers to a pool of global fixed income investors across Asia, Europe and the US.

  • Support for compliance and finance processes relating to deal management, and preparation of internal strategy presentations, as needed.

What qualities and skills are we looking for?

  • Solid background in accounting and finance

  • Analytical mind with strong attention to detail

  • Ability to coordinate with multiple parties

  • Strong motivation and good team player

  • Preference for candidates who are available for 6-month internship

What would you gain from this internship?

  • Daily exposure on global macroeconomic developments and primary bond market (i.e. USD, EUR, and select local ASEAN currencies)

  • Collaboration with other banking functions such as sustainable finance, sector and in-country teams / relationship management, financial markets, corporate finance, legal, and risk management / compliance.
